Imagine an object unwinding – maybe some yarn, some bubbles, or some knots that you place beside you. Once you’ve placed them all, give yourself a minute to look at them all. You don’t have to change anything, but you can label them if you need to (just a word or two). How many did you put down? Which one do you need to work on, and what does it need – warmth, protection, action? Keep one strand in your attention and put the others somewhere you can see them and return.

parts.name: Pay attention to the sounds in the room you’re in and how yo...
parts.text: Pay attention to the sounds in the room you’re in and how your body feels, then imagine yourself walking somewhere. Where do you want to go? Listen to the sounds of your footsteps and take in your surroundings as you walk. What do objects feel like if you touch them? What landmarks do you see? When you feel you have gathered enough of your attention, imagine the scenery changing until you are in a place where you can talk to whoever you need to (or you can just cut to the chase, if you prefer). Pay attention to something without worrying about what it means. Allow yourself to be curious about what’s going to happen next, but don’t make it a “what are they going to do to you?” kind of thing. When you are ready to finish, imagine yourself walking back the way you came and close the space.

parts.name: Start with a very small neutral area, feel into it a little...
parts.text: Start with a very small neutral area, feel into it a little and then imagine a wave of warmth, steadiness, or attention spreading out to a new area that is still ok. Sense into the new area (or continue using the old). See if there is anything different at each step. Does the body want any contact, space, words, other care? Let the mental image go, sense your body, sense your contact points, come back.

parts.name: Prepare the workshop (time, place, tools, boundaries, etc)....
parts.text: Prepare the workshop (time, place, tools, boundaries, etc). Invite the signal/feeling/young part to come only as close as is welcome. Try to avoid any language that makes you feel you’re not one person. Care for it as best you can, by asking what it wants and giving that if you can, or sensing into it and responding, or just being with it. Take breaks, get back in contact if that’s ok, take more breaks, etc. Keep bringing in adult functions (or borrow someone else’s function). Have the adult part of you run the show. The goal is to make it “good as you” rather than “good as new”, not to erase history. Tell your little one, “That’s enough for today. We’re going back to the life we’re building.” Close the workspace, reassure yourself that you are one whole person, that you’re an adult now, and come back.

Come back, keeping the quality and a positive action that you would do with it, but leaving the imagined you behind, saying “I am me”.
